correctness.rationale: For an irredundant full-dimensional compact polytope, the facet-interior point p_i has strict slack against all other facets, so s>0. A closed translate excluding query y must be contained in some strict facet halfspace, giving one inequality. With compact support in an R-ball, t>=2R/s, a facet-aligned translate at h< <u_i,y> contains exactly the support halfspace slice <=h; continuity from below handles positive atoms on the query plane and yields all-y equality with closed halfspace survival mass. For continuous everywhere-positive densities, a bounded maximizing translated polytope has strictly less mass than its containing halfspace, so no finite t matches the limit. Independently verified facet-slack algebra and inspected rational-coordinate witness checker; tests are corroborative, not all-measure proof.
